newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes lower, palladium stretches gains.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes lower, palladium stretches gains.

text.p: Gold prices fixed easier on Wednesday as the market edged back within its established range of $347.00-$350.00 per ounce, but palladium extended its gains to a fresh 21-month high, dealers said.
Gold fixed at $348.00, down $1.10 from Tuesday, after receiving little support from the New York and Far East markets.
"It seems to be moving lower and I would not be surprised if we re-visit the recent lows (around $336)," one dealer said.
Equally, he added, it would be no surprise to see bullion trade at $350.00 ahead of the Comex option expiry, due after the close of business on Friday.
Palladium fixed at a fresh 21-month high of $157.75, $3.75 ahead of its Tuesday afternoon setting. Its previous top since July 10, 1995 was $157.50 on March 11 this year.
Dealers noted that the nearby palladium supplies had tightened to the extent that the market had moved into a backwardation of around $10 this month.
"There is a lot of Japanese interest," one dealer said, referring to the consequence of Russian-Japanese supply contracts for this year remaining unsigned.
Lease rates have also soared, with one month quoted at 10 percent, from six percent on Tuesday.

Russia, the world's leading palladium exporter, and Japan, the major importer, have yet to discuss contracts for supplies which ended in November last year. No palladium exports licences have been signed by the Russian prime minister and no exports are forecast this month or next, according to Russian officials.
Japanese importers have been buying on the dealer market, pushing up prices and attracting the attention of speculators, whose interest has firmed prices further.
"There has been a lot of buying by one or two parties but they have not been lending, which has pushed out the backwardation," one dealer said.
By a little over an hour after it fixed, palladium had slipped a couple of dollars to $155.00/$156.00, still up $1.50 on the previous close.
Its sister metal platinum was much less moved and was indicated unchanged at $365.00/$366.00 in the middle of an overall $360-$370 range.
Silver was under some pressure at $4.76/$4.78, down two cents, and possibly heading for its $4.72 support after retracing from a $4.83 high on Tuesday, dealers said.
